meanings.note: Literal eye (gli occhi del cuore); singular occhio che... warns someone to be careful.
Contraction of preposition di + masculine singular article il.

examples.trans: It is not from your department.

meanings.note: Literal organ and figurative seat of passion (mettere il cuore).

examples.trans: Let us put our heart into the work.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.
Compound cardinal numeral (cento + sessanta + otto), used here as a scene number.
Ordinal adjective; on a film slate, feminines prima / seconda stand for prima ripresa ('first take').

examples.text: Ho visto le prime due puntate.
examples.trans: I watched the first two episodes.

meanings.note: Director's cue starting a take on set; also an act or deed.

examples.trans: We swing into action right away.

meanings.note: Before a plural noun (certe volte), means 'some / certain'.
Used alone as an emphatic affirmative reply.

examples.trans: Of course, I am coming right away!

meanings.note: Countable 'time' (certe volte, 'sometimes'), unlike tempo (uncountable time or weather).
Ownership, age (avere venti anni), and idioms like avere voglia di.
Forms compound past tenses of transitive verbs.
Avere voglia di + infinitive means 'to feel like doing something'.

examples.trans: I feel like having a coffee.
I would feel like going away.

meanings.note: Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.

ricominciare.gloss: to start again; to begin anew

meanings.en: to start over; to begin again
meanings.note: Prefix ri- ('again') + cominciare.

examples.trans: Let us start everything all over again.

meanings.note: Singular tutto alone means 'everything'; masculine plural tutti alone means 'everyone'.
Origin in space or time (da casa, da oggi, da capo).
Before a person's name (vai da Duccio), means going to where they are.

examples.trans: I am going over to Arianna's.

meanings.note: Literally 'head'; da capo means from the beginning or all over again.

examples.trans: Let us start from the top.

meanings.note: Movement away from the speaker or toward a destination.
Used in expressions like va bene, ti va, or andare male.
Location or state; in silenzio means quietly, in porta means in goal.
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
Slightly more literary or reflective synonym of posto.

examples.trans: I am looking for a quiet place.

meanings.note: Before the noun often means 'another / newly arrived' (il nuovo stagista); after the noun, 'brand-new / unfamiliar' (un luogo nuovo).

examples.trans: I am looking for a new place.

meanings.note: Interrogative and relative adverb of place; elides to dov' before è.

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the exit?

meanings.note: Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Unstressed 1st-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun (mi sento, mi piace, mi serve).

conoscere.gloss: to know; to be acquainted with

meanings.en: to know (a person, place, or feeling)
meanings.note: Familiarity through experience, unlike sapere (to know facts or skills).
Pairs with non before the verb: non mi conosce nessuno.

sapere.gloss: to know (a fact or how to)

meanings.note: Knowing facts or answers (sa dov'è?, non lo so).
Followed directly by an infinitive (sai giocare?, 'do you know how to play?').

examples.trans: Do you know how to play foosball?

meanings.note: Used both transitively (cambiare canale) and intransitively (le cose cambiano).
Invariable noun ending in a stressed vowel.
First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
Near demonstrative; colloquially questa alone can refer brusquely to 'this woman / she'.
An inner impression or emotional feeling.
Builds general statements (non si fuma, i copioni si cambiano).
Third-person reflexive pronoun (si chiama, si è svegliata, non si preoccupi).
Contact someone by voice or telephone.
With mi/ti/si, expresses someone's or something's name.
Used both literally for height and figuratively for personal growth.
Invariable cardinal number (venti + quattro).
Unit of calendar time; used with avere to state someone's age.
Shouted by an Italian director to end or abort a camera take.
Invariable cardinal number (trenta + quattro).
Modal verb followed directly by an infinitive.

examples.trans: I have to talk to you.

meanings.note: Irregular verb; past participle detto, familiar imperative di' (fused in dille, 'tell her').
Negative reply; in se no ('if not'), means 'otherwise'.

examples.trans: Run, otherwise you will be late.

meanings.note: Imperatives match address: scusa / scusami (informal tu), scusi (polite lei), scusate (plural voi).

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the exit?

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction introducing contrast or surprise (ma guarda!, ma come?).

examples.trans: I wanted to come, but I am working.

meanings.note: Question word asking manner or requesting repetition (Come, scusa?).
Introduces a comparison.
Friendly or impatient encouragement built from dare.
Prefix ri- + irregular fare; rifacciamola attaches object la ('let us redo it').

examples.trans: Come on, let us reshoot the scene.
I need to remake the coffee.

potere.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; may; to be able to
meanings.note: Modal verb expressing ability or permission.
Infinitive drops final -e when a pronoun attaches: obbligarmi ('to force me').
Stressed pronoun after prepositions (con me) and clitic form before li/lo/la/ne (me ne danno, me li sento).
Partitive clitic replacing a counted noun (ne ho ventiquattro, 'I have twenty-four of them [years]').
Part of andarsene (te ne vai, 'you leave / walk away').

examples.text: Quanti anni hai? Ne ho venti.
examples.trans: How old are you? I am twenty.

meanings.note: Also used idiomatically: darsi del tu (use informal 'you'), dare venti anni (guess someone's age).
Introduces a logical result in speech and writing.

examples.trans: It is raining, so I am staying home.
It is late, so let us go.

meanings.note: Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Actor's or director's shooting script in theatre, film, and television.

examples.trans: The scripts are on the table.

meanings.note: Default masculine plural definite article, plural of il.
Parlare con means speaking with someone; parlare male di means criticising.

examples.trans: I need to talk to you.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment, instrument, or attitude.
Literally a fishing or goal net; in broadcasting, the TV network commissioning a show.

examples.trans: The ball lands in the net.

meanings.note: Default masculine singular definite article before most consonants.
Drops final -e before a surname (il dottor Cane); used in Italy as a respectful title for executives.

examples.text: Il dottor Rossi è al telefono.
examples.trans: Dr Rossi is on the phone.

meanings.note: Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner/pronoun; before masculine nouns adapts like lo/il: quel, quell', quello, quei, quegli.

examples.trans: Do you see those light stands?

meanings.note: Expresses desire or intention; imperfect volevo softens a polite request.
Shortens to buon before most masculine nouns; on set, Buona! approves a take.
Used in wishes such as Buona serata! ('Have a nice evening!').
